hook.text: A METAR is a routine weather observation from an airport—compressed into a coded line that pilots decode instantly.

buildup.text: It reports wind, visibility, weather phenomena, clouds, temperature, dewpoint, and altimeter setting—all in one string.

discovery.text: METARs are issued hourly or when conditions change significantly—SPECIs are special reports for rapid changes.

twist.text: The format is standardized worldwide by ICAO—a pilot from Japan can read a METAR from Brazil without translation.

climax.text: Automated stations (ASOS/AWOS) generate METARs continuously—but human observers still add value for clouds and weather.

punchline.text: One coded line—and a pilot knows the airport's weather.
